rationale: The Latin anchors *fragorem edere* (to make a crashing/cracking sound), *sonare* (to sound), and *crepare* (to crack, creak, burst) point to a sense of breaking apart suddenly with noise. Among the candidates, burst.v.08 ("break open or apart suddenly and forcefully") most closely captures this physical, violent rupturing action attested in the Beowulf and Exodus passages, while the noise element is supported by *crepare/sonare* and is consistent with the breaking-apart sense rather than a purely acoustic one.
